A bar magnet with magnetic moment \( 2.4 \, \text{A m}^2 \) is placed at a distance of \( 0.6 \, \text{m} \) along its axis. What is the magnetic field \( B \) at that point? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
In a purely resistive AC circuit, the phase difference between voltage and current is:

text_solutions:
For a pure resistor, \( v = v_m \sin \omega t \) and \( i = i_m \sin \omega t \).

Phase difference \( \phi = 0^\circ \), as they are in phase.

qns_content.text: The electric field of an EM wave oscillates with amplitude \( 48 \, \text{V/m} \) and frequency \( 2 \times 10^{10} \, \text{Hz} \). What is the amplitude of the magnetic field? (Given \( c = 3 \times 10^8 \, \text{m/s} \))

A solenoid produces \( B = 0.85 \, \text{T} \) with a core of \( \mu_r = 200 \) and \( n = 1500 \, \text{m}^{-1} \). What is the current \( I \)? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
A paramagnetic material with \( \chi = 2 \times 10^{-3} \) is placed in \( H = 500 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \). What is \( M \)?

Two parallel wires \( 0.02 \, \text{m} \) apart carry \( 10 \, \text{A} \) and \( 3 \, \text{A} \) in the same direction. What is the force per unit length? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
Which of the following equations is dimensionally inconsistent?
A stone falls from a height of \( 72 \, \text{m} \) on a planet and takes \( 3 \, \text{s} \) to reach the ground. What is the gravitational acceleration on this planet?

A charged conductor has a surface charge density of \( 2 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{C/m}^2 \). What is the electric field just outside it? (Take \( \varepsilon_0 = 8.85 \times 10^{-12} \, \text{C}^2 \text{N}^{-1} \text{m}^{-2} \)).

A conductor has a resistivity of \( 3 \times 10^{-8} \, \Omega \text{m} \) and \( \alpha = 4 \times 10^{-3} \, ^\circ\text{C}^{-1} \) at \( 25^\circ \text{C} \). What is its resistivity at \( 75^\circ \text{C} \)?

An electron moves with a speed of \( 4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m/s} \) perpendicular to a magnetic field of \( 0.3 \, \text{T} \). What is the radius of its path? (Mass = \( 9.1 \times 10^{-31} \, \text{kg} \), charge = \( 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \, \text{C} \))

A bar magnet produces a field of \( 3 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{T} \) at \( 0.6 \, \text{m} \) on its equatorial line. What is its magnetic moment? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
A solenoid of 1000 turns/m and area 0.02 m² has \( \mu_r = 2 \). What is its self-inductance? (\( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{H/m} \))
A wire of length \( 4 \, \text{m} \) and resistance \( 8 \, \Omega \) is stretched to double its length. What is its new resistance?

text_solutions:
Resistance: \( R = \frac{\rho l}{A} \). Volume \( l A \) is constant.

New length: \( l' = 2l \), new area: \( A' = \frac{A}{2} \).

New resistance: \( R' = \frac{\rho (2l)}{\frac{A}{2}} = \frac{4 \rho l}{A} = 4R = 4 \times 8 = 32 \, \Omega \).

qns_content.text: What is the SI unit of a quantity with dimensional formula \( [M L T^{-1}] \)?

text_solutions:
\( [M] = \text{kg}, [L] = \text{m}, [T] = \text{s} \).

\( [M L T^{-1}] = \text{kg m s}^{-1} \).

(Matches momentum or impulse).

qns_content.text: A brass plate of area 0.04 m2 experiences a shearing force of 2 × 104 N. If the shear strain is 1 × 10-5, what is the shear modulus of brass?

text_solutions:
Shear modulus: G = (Shear stress) / (Shear strain).

Shear stress: Shear stress = F / A = (2 × 104) / 0.04 = 5 × 105 N/m2.

Shear strain: 1 × 10-5.

Substitute: G = (5 × 105) / (1 × 10-5) = 5 × 1010 N/m2.

qns_content.text: What is the molar specific heat capacity at constant pressure for a diatomic gas if \( C_v = \frac{5}{2} R \) and \( R = 8.3 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \)?
What is the pressure exerted by 1 mole of an ideal gas in a 10-litre container at 300 K? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
A simple pendulum has a period of \( 4 \, \text{s} \) on Earth. What is its period on a planet with \( g = 4.9 \, \text{m/s}^2 \)? (\( g_{\text{Earth}} = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
A wire has a resistance of \( 20 \, \Omega \) at \( 30^\circ \text{C} \) and \( 22 \, \Omega \) at \( 80^\circ \text{C} \). What is the temperature coefficient of resistivity?

A circuit has a \( 20 \, \text{V} \) battery with \( 2 \, \Omega \) internal resistance and three resistors \( 5 \, \Omega \), \( 10 \, \Omega \), \( 20 \, \Omega \) in parallel. What is the current through the \( 10 \, \Omega \) resistor?

A car accelerates from rest at \( 3 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 5 \, \text{s} \), then decelerates at \( 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) until its speed is \( 9 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the total distance covered?
A force starts at \( 80 \, \text{N} \) over \( 6 \, \text{m} \), then decreases linearly to \( 20 \, \text{N} \) over \( 9 \, \text{m} \). What is the total work done?
What is the Kelvin temperature equivalent to \( 45^\circ \text{F} \)?

A disk rotates at \( 5 \, \text{rad/s} \) with a moment of inertia \( 2 \, \text{kg m}^2 \). If an external torque of \( 10 \, \text{Nm} \) acts for \( 2 \, \text{s} \), what is the final angular velocity?

A moon orbits a planet with period 5 days and radius \( 2 \times 10^8 \, \text{m} \). What is the planet’s mass? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2, 1 \, \text{day} = 86400 \, \text{s} \))
A force starts at \( 100 \, \text{N} \) over \( 4 \, \text{m} \), then decreases linearly to \( 30 \, \text{N} \) over \( 6 \, \text{m} \). What is the total work done?

A submarine window (\( 0.03 \, \text{m}^2 \)) is at \( 500 \, \text{m} \) depth in seawater (\( \rho = 1.03 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)). What force acts on it if inside pressure is atmospheric? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))

An aluminium wire of length \( 1.8 \, \text{m} \) and cross-sectional area \( 3 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \) is stretched by a force of \( 300 \, \text{N} \). If the Young's modulus of aluminium is \( 7 \times 10^{10} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the elongation?
A spring-mass system oscillates with \( T = 0.8 \, \text{s} \) when \( m = 0.2 \, \text{kg} \). What is the spring constant?
A plane sheet has a surface charge density \( \sigma = 3.54 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{C/m}^2 \). What is the electric field magnitude near it?
A tank of water (refractive index = 1.33) has a depth of \( 20 \, \text{cm} \). What is the apparent depth when viewed normally?

text_solutions:
Apparent depth = \( \frac{\text{real depth}}{n} \).

Real depth = \( 20 \, \text{cm} \), \( n = 1.33 \).

Apparent depth = \( \frac{20}{1.33} \approx 15.04 \, \text{cm} \).

qns_content.text: A transverse wave travels on a string with tension 50 N and linear mass density 0.02 kg/m. What is the wavelength if the frequency is 25 Hz?
A train moving at \( 36 \, \text{km/h} \) accelerates at \( 0.5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 20 \, \text{s} \), then decelerates at \( 1 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) to rest. What is the total distance covered?
In a double-slit experiment, what is the distance of the second bright fringe from the central maximum if \( \lambda = 500 \, \text{nm} \), \( d = 0.2 \, \text{mm} \), and \( D = 1.0 \, \text{m} \)?

Light of frequency \( 5.0 \times 10^{14} \, \text{Hz} \) is incident on a metal surface with work function \( 1.8 \, \text{eV} \). What is the maximum speed of emitted electrons? (Take \( h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34} \, \text{J s} \), \( m_e = 9.11 \times 10^{-31} \, \text{kg} \))
Light of wavelength \( 350 \, \text{nm} \) is incident on a metal with work function \( 2.0 \, \text{eV} \). What is the stopping potential? (Take \( h c = 1240 \, \text{eV nm} \))
A projectile is launched at \( 10 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 37^\circ \). What is its vertical velocity after \( 1 \, \text{s} \)? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2, \sin 37^\circ = 0.6 \))
An electron in a hydrogen atom is excited to \( n = 3 \) and then falls to \( n = 1 \). What is the maximum energy of the emitted photon? (Use \( E_n = -\frac{13.6}{n^2} \, \text{eV} \))
What is the nuclear density if a nucleus has a mass of \( 9.27 \times 10^{-26} \, \text{kg} \) and volume of \( 4.05 \times 10^{-44} \, \text{m}^3 \)?
A \( 0.3 \, \text{kg} \) stone is whirled at \( 50 \, \text{rev/min} \) in a circle of radius \( 2 \, \text{m} \) with a \( 5 \, \text{N} \) tangential force. What is the net force at that instant?
Which process balances diffusion current in a p-n junction at equilibrium?

text_solutions: At equilibrium, the diffusion current due to carrier concentration gradients is balanced by the drift current caused by the electric field in the depletion region, resulting in no net current.

qns_content.text: A \( 5 \, \text{kg} \) block on a \( 37^\circ \) incline (\( \mu_k = 0.2 \)) is pulled upward by a \( 7 \, \text{kg} \) mass over a pulley. What is the tension? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( \sin 37^\circ = 0.6 \), \( \cos 37^\circ = 0.8 \))
The ionic radius of \(F^-\) is larger than that of F because:

text_solutions: Adding an electron to F forms \(F^-\), increasing electron repulsion and decreasing effective nuclear charge, thus increasing radius.

qns_content.text: Which of the following ions achieves a stable octet configuration by gaining one electron?

text_solutions: Chlorine (\( \ce{Cl} \), \( 3s^2 3p^5 \)) has 7 valence electrons. Gaining one electron forms \( \ce{Cl^-} \) (\( 3s^2 3p^6 \)), achieving an octet like argon.

qns_content.text: Which compound involves ionic bonding between a group 2 element and a group 17 element?

text_solutions: \( \ce{MgCl2} \) forms by electron transfer from magnesium (group 2) to chlorine (group 17), creating \( \ce{Mg^2+} \) and \( \ce{Cl^-} \).

qns_content.text: Calculate the heat absorbed by 18 g of water to vaporize at 373 K, given \(\Delta_{vap} H^\circ = 40.79 kJ/mol\) (molar mass of water = 18 g/mol).

text_solutions: Moles = \(18 / 18 = 1 mol\). Heat absorbed = \(n \times \Delta_{vap} H^\circ = 1 \times 40.79 = 40.79 kJ\).

qns_content.text: For an exothermic reaction \( \ce{A <=> B} \), adding a catalyst will:

text_solutions: A catalyst increases the rate of both forward and reverse reactions equally, not affecting the equilibrium position.

qns_content.text: What is the oxidation number of Cl in \( \ce{ClO3^-} \)?
In the Dumas method, 0.5 g of a compound gave 112 mL of \( \ce{N2} \) at STP. What is the percentage of nitrogen? (Atomic mass: N = 14)

What is the degree of dissociation of 0.025 M methanoic acid if its molar conductivity is 46.1 S cm² mol⁻¹, given \( \lambda^0(\text{H}^+) = 349.6 \, \text{S cm}^2 \text{mol}^{-1} \) and \( \lambda^0(\text{HCOO}^-) = 54.6 \, \text{S cm}^2 \text{mol}^{-1} \)?
The rate law of a reaction is \( \ce{Rate = k[A][B]^2} \). If [A] is doubled and [B] is halved, what happens to the rate?
Which of the following is a purine base?

text_solutions: Adenine is a purine base (two-ring structure) found in both DNA and RNA, unlike pyrimidine bases (single-ring) like thymine or uracil.

qns_content.text: Which compound exhibits metamerism with \( \ce{CH3CH2OCH2CH3} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH3CH2OCH2CH3} \) (diethyl ether) has the formula \( \ce{C4H10O} \). \( \ce{CH3OCH2CH2CH3} \) (methyl propyl ether) has the same formula but different alkyl groups around the ether oxygen.

qns_content.text: Calculate \(\Delta G^\circ\) for a reaction at 298 K if \(K = 1000\) (R = 8.314 J/mol·K).
Which molecule exhibits intermolecular hydrogen bonding in its liquid state?

text_solutions: \( \ce{H2O} \) forms intermolecular hydrogen bonds between hydrogen and oxygen of different molecules, unlike \( \ce{CH4} \) or \( \ce{Cl2} \).

qns_content.text: What is the electronic configuration of chromium (Z = 24), considering its exceptional stability?

text_solutions: Chromium’s configuration is 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d⁵ 4s¹ instead of 3d⁴ 4s² due to the extra stability of a half-filled 3d subshell.

qns_content.text: What is the mass of one mole of ethanol (C₂H₅OH)? (Atomic masses: C = 12, H = 1, O = 16)

text_solutions: Molar mass = (2 × 12) + (6 × 1) + 16 = 46 g/mol.

qns_content.text: What is the pH of a 0.001 M \( \ce{Ba(OH)2} \) solution, assuming complete dissociation?
In combustion analysis, 0.36 g of a compound gave 0.36 g of \( \ce{H2O} \). What is the percentage of hydrogen? (Atomic masses: H = 1, O = 16)
The Henry's law constant for a gas in water is \( 4 \times 10^4 \, \text{bar} \) at 298 K. What is the mole fraction of the gas under a partial pressure of 2 bar?
What is the molar conductivity at infinite dilution for MgSO₄ if the ionic molar conductivities of Mg²⁺ and SO₄²⁻ are 106.0 S cm² mol⁻¹ and 160.0 S cm² mol⁻¹ respectively?
The rate constant of a reaction is \( 3.0 \times 10^{-3} \, \ce{s^{-1}} \) at 25°C and \( E_a = 62 \, \ce{kJ mol^{-1}} \). What is the rate constant at 35°C? (R = 8.314 J/mol·K)
Which lanthanoid ion has a \( 4f^7 \) configuration and exhibits paramagnetism?

text_solutions: Gd (Z = 64) forms \( \ce{Gd^{3+}} \) with \( 4f^7 \), having 7 unpaired electrons, making it paramagnetic.

qns_content.text: Which complex shows ionization isomerism with \( \ce{[Co(NH3)5SO4]Br} \)?

text_solutions: Ionization isomerism involves different ions outside the coordination sphere. \( \ce{[Co(NH3)5Br]SO4} \) is an ionization isomer of \( \ce{[Co(NH3)5SO4]Br} \), as \( \ce{Br^-} \) and \( \ce{SO4^{2-}} \) switch positions.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a geminal dihalide?

text_solutions: Geminal dihalides have both halogens attached to the same carbon atom.

qns_content.text: Which reagent is used to convert benzene into benzaldehyde?

text_solutions: The Gattermann-Koch reaction involves carbon monoxide and HCl in the presence of anhydrous \(\ce{AlCl3}\) and \(\ce{CuCl}\) to form benzaldehyde.

qns_content.text: Which of the following compounds will give a positive Schiff’s test?

text_solutions: Schiff’s test is used to detect aldehydes. Aldehydes react with Schiff’s reagent to give a pink or magenta color, while ketones do not.

qns_content.text: The lanthanoid with the highest atomic number is:

text_solutions: Lutetium (Lu, Z = 71) is the last lanthanoid, with the highest atomic number in the series.

qns_content.text: For the reaction \( \ce{A + 2B -> 3C} \), the rate of formation of C is \( 1.5 \times 10^{-3} \, \ce{mol L^{-1} s^{-1}} \). What is the rate of disappearance of B?
Which among the following hydrocarbons is most reactive?

text_solutions: Alkynes are more reactive than alkenes and alkanes due to the presence of a triple bond.

qns_content.text: Which purification technique is best suited for separating a mixture of liquids based on their adsorption properties?

text_solutions: Chromatography separates compounds based on their differential adsorption on a stationary phase (e.g., silica) and movement with a mobile phase.

qns_content.text: What is the mass percentage of sulfur in Na₂S₂O₃? (Atomic masses: Na = 23, S = 32, O = 16)
Which atomic model could not explain the stability of an atom due to electron radiation?

text_solutions: Rutherford’s model likened electrons to planets orbiting the nucleus, but classical mechanics predicts they would radiate energy and collapse, failing to explain stability.

qns_content.text: Which of the following ions has a \( 3d^7 \) configuration?

text_solutions: Co (Z = 27) has \( 3d^7 4s^2 \). For \( \ce{Co^{2+}} \), 2 electrons from 4s are lost, leaving \( 3d^7 \).

qns_content.text: Which ligand is strongest in the spectrochemical series among the following?

text_solutions: The spectrochemical series orders ligands by field strength: \( \ce{I^-} < \ce{Cl^-} < \ce{H2O} < \ce{CN^-} \). \( \ce{CN^-} \) is the strongest field ligand here.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about alcohols is incorrect?

options.text: Alcohols have higher boiling points than ethers

text_solutions: Alcohols are generally more acidic than water, but the presence of alkyl groups reduces acidity.

qns_content.text: Which of the following hydrides is formed by a Group 15 element?

text_solutions: Group 15 elements (ns²np³) form hydrides like NH₃ (nitrogen), unlike Group 1 (LiH), Group 2 (MgH₂), or Group 14 (CH₄).

qns_content.text: For \( \ce{N2(g) + 3H2(g) <=> 2NH3(g)} \), removing \( \ce{NH3} \) will:

text_solutions: By Le Chatelier’s principle, removing \( \ce{NH3} \) shifts the equilibrium to the right to produce more \( \ce{NH3} \).

qns_content.text: Which of the following compounds will show geometrical isomerism?

text_solutions: Alkenes of the type \( \ce{C=C} \) with two different groups attached to each carbon exhibit geometrical isomerism.

qns_content.text: A gas has a solubility of 0.015 mol/L in water at a partial pressure of 3 bar at 298 K. What is the Henry's law constant (\( K_H \)) in bar?

text_solutions:
Henry's law: \( p = K_H \cdot \text{solubility (in molarity)} \).

\( K_H = \frac{p}{\text{solubility}} = \frac{3}{0.015} = 200 \, \text{bar} \).

qns_content.text: What is the hybridization of the carbon atom in an allylic halide?

text_solutions: In allylic halides, the halogen is attached to an sp3-hybridized carbon adjacent to a carbon-carbon double bond.

qns_content.text: Which reaction is used to introduce an -OH group at the ortho position of phenol?

text_solutions: Kolbe’s reaction involves the reaction of sodium phenoxide with CO2 to introduce an -OH group at the ortho position.

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{(CH3)2NH} \) reacts with \( \ce{HNO2} \)?

text_solutions: Secondary amines like \( \ce{(CH3)2NH} \) react with \( \ce{HNO2} \) to form yellow oily N-nitrosoamines, \( \ce{(CH3)2N-N=O} \), without gas evolution.

qns_content.text: Which of the following vitamins is also known as ascorbic acid?

text_solutions: Vitamin C, a water-soluble vitamin, is chemically known as ascorbic acid and prevents scurvy by aiding collagen synthesis.

qns_content.text: How many grams of ethylene glycol (\( \ce{C2H6O2} \)) are required to depress the freezing point of 300 g of water by 1.24 K? (\( K_f = 1.86 \, \text{K kg/mol}, \text{Molar mass of ethylene glycol} = 62 \, \text{g/mol} \))
Which of the following amines reacts with \( \ce{CH3COCl} \) to form an amide?

text_solutions: Primary amines like \( \ce{CH3CH2NH2} \) react with acetyl chloride (\( \ce{CH3COCl} \)) to form amides (\( \ce{CH3CONHCH2CH3} \)), while tertiary amines do not.

qns_content.text: What is the molality of a solution containing 8 g of NaOH in 400 g of water? (Molar mass of NaOH = 40 g/mol)

text_solutions:
Moles = 8 / 40 = 0.2 mol.

Mass of solvent = 0.4 kg.

Molality = 0.2 / 0.4 = 0.5 m.

qns_content.text: Which plastid type is responsible for storing oils and fats?

text_solutions: Elaioplasts are specialized leucoplasts responsible for storing oils and fats in plant cells.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is an example of a monocarpic plant?

text_solutions: Monocarpic plants, like bamboo, flower once in their lifetime and die after producing seeds.

qns_content.text: Which stage of mitosis is characterized by the reappearance of the nuclear envelope?

text_solutions: During telophase, the nuclear envelope reforms around separated chromosome sets, completing nuclear division.

qns_content.text: What is the term for the ability of cells to differentiate into specific tissues based on their position within an organ?

text_solutions: Open differentiation refers to the ability of plant cells to develop different structures based on their positional information.

qns_content.text: In flowering plants, the structure that contains the ovules is known as the:

text_solutions: The ovary is the part of the carpel that encloses the ovules and later develops into a fruit after fertilization.

qns_content.text: Which age pyramid shape indicates a rapidly growing population?

text_solutions: A broad-based triangular age pyramid indicates a high birth rate and a rapidly growing population.

qns_content.text: Which law of inheritance states that alleles separate independently during gamete formation?

text_solutions: The Law of Independent Assortment states that different gene pairs assort independently during gamete formation.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about a dihybrid cross is correct?

options.text: It studies the inheritance of two genes simultaneously.
It follows only the Law of Segregation.
It involves only one pair of contrasting traits.
It always produces offspring with identical phenotypes.

text_solutions: A dihybrid cross studies the inheritance of two different genes at the same time.

qns_content.text: Which part of a flowering plant is primarily responsible for food storage?

text_solutions: Food storage occurs in different parts of plants, including roots (carrot), stems (potato), and leaves (cabbage).

qns_content.text: What is the primary purpose of biological classification?

text_solutions: Classification helps categorize organisms into convenient groups based on shared characteristics.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of isobilateral (monocot) leaves?

options.text: Stomata are present only on the lower epidermis
Mesophyll is differentiated into palisade and spongy layers
Bulliform cells help in rolling the leaves

text_solutions: Bulliform cells in monocot leaves help in rolling the leaves during water stress to minimize water loss.

qns_content.text: What is the primary function of the rough endoplasmic reticulum?

text_solutions: The rough endoplasmic reticulum, with ribosomes attached, is primarily involved in protein synthesis.

qns_content.text: In which phase of meiosis does crossing over occur?

text_solutions: Crossing over occurs during prophase I of meiosis, allowing genetic recombination between homologous chromosomes.

qns_content.text: In which cell organelle does photorespiration partly occur?

text_solutions: Photorespiration involves three organelles: chloroplast, peroxisome, and mitochondrion.

qns_content.text: What is the final phase of the plant growth curve where growth rate declines and stabilizes?

text_solutions: In the stationary phase, the growth rate declines and stabilizes, marking the final phase of the sigmoid curve.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a function of rRNA?

options.text: Forms the structural and catalytic part of ribosomes.
Acts as a template for DNA replication.

text_solutions: rRNA forms the structural and catalytic part of ribosomes, playing a key role in translation.

qns_content.text: Which of the following correctly describes a test cross?

options.text: A cross between an unknown genotype and a homozygous recessive

text_solutions: A test cross helps determine an unknown genotype by crossing with a homozygous recessive.

qns_content.text: What is the significance of double fertilization in angiosperms?

options.text: It ensures the formation of two zygotes.
It results in the formation of a diploid embryo and a triploid endosperm.
It produces an embryo and a seed coat.
It prevents the occurrence of genetic variation.

text_solutions: Double fertilization is unique to flowering plants; one sperm fuses with the egg to form a diploid zygote, while the other fuses with the two polar nuclei to form a triploid endosperm, which nourishes the developing embryo.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about the respiratory quotient (RQ) is CORRECT?

options.text: RQ has no relation to the type of respiratory substrate.

text_solutions: When carbohydrates are used as respiratory substrates, the RQ value is 1.

qns_content.text: What is the nature of genetic material in most plant viruses?

text_solutions: Most plant viruses have single-stranded RNA as their genetic material.

qns_content.text: How does the presence of stolons help certain plants in vegetative propagation?

options.text: They grow upward and produce new flowers
They spread horizontally and form new plants at nodes
They store food and support the parent plant

text_solutions: Stolons, such as those found in strawberries, grow horizontally and give rise to new plants at nodes, facilitating vegetative propagation.

qns_content.text: Which cells in plants regulate transpiration?

text_solutions: Guard cells regulate the opening and closing of stomata, thereby controlling transpiration in plants.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about the cytoskeleton is incorrect?

options.text: The cytoskeleton provides structural support to the cell.
The cytoskeleton is composed of microtubules, microfilaments, and intermediate filaments.
The cytoskeleton is involved in intracellular transport.

text_solutions: The cytoskeleton is not involved in ribosome production; it provides support and aids in cell movement and transport.

qns_content.text: What marks the end of telophase in mitosis?

text_solutions: At the end of telophase, the nuclear membrane reforms around the newly separated daughter chromosomes.

qns_content.text: What is the function of ATP and NADPH in the Calvin cycle?

text_solutions: ATP provides energy, and NADPH provides reducing power for the conversion of CO₂ into carbohydrates in the Calvin cycle.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about tRNA is incorrect?

options.text: tRNA contains an anticodon that pairs with mRNA codons.
tRNA carries amino acids to the ribosome.
tRNA is synthesized by RNA polymerase II.

text_solutions: tRNA is synthesized by RNA polymerase III, not RNA polymerase II.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is NOT a factor affecting population size?

text_solutions: Climate stability does not directly regulate population size, whereas natality, mortality, and migration influence population dynamics.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is NOT a major cause of biodiversity loss?

text_solutions: While habitat destruction, pollution, and climate change contribute to biodiversity loss, an increase in mutation rates does not significantly impact biodiversity loss.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about sex-linked inheritance is incorrect?

options.text: Color blindness is an X-linked recessive disorder.
Y-linked traits are only inherited by male offspring.
Hemophilia follows an X-linked recessive inheritance pattern.

text_solutions: Females can inherit X-linked disorders if they receive two copies of the affected allele.

qns_content.text: Which of the following fungal groups is commonly known as 'club fungi'?

text_solutions: Basidiomycetes are known as 'club fungi' because of their club-shaped reproductive structures called basidia.

qns_content.text: Which of the following adaptations is most commonly found in floating aquatic plants?

text_solutions: Floating aquatic plants have aerenchyma, a specialized parenchyma with air spaces that provide buoyancy.

qns_content.text: Which type of simple permanent tissue makes up the majority of the cortex in dicot roots?

text_solutions: The cortex of dicot roots consists mostly of parenchymatous cells, which store food and provide structural support.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about chromatin is correct?

options.text: Chromatin is composed of RNA and lipids.
Chromatin consists of DNA and histone proteins.
Chromatin is found only in prokaryotic cells.

text_solutions: Chromatin is a complex of DNA and histone proteins found in the nucleus of eukaryotic cells.

qns_content.text: Which of the following structures is absent during prophase?

text_solutions: During prophase, the nucleolus disappears, and the chromatin condenses into visible chromosomes.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of C₄ plants?

options.text: They have a single carbon fixation step

text_solutions: C₄ plants have high water-use efficiency due to their ability to minimize photorespiration.

qns_content.text: Which compound is the primary electron donor in cellular respiration?

text_solutions: NADH donates electrons to the electron transport chain, playing a crucial role in cellular respiration.

qns_content.text: Which conservation strategy is used for critically endangered species with very small populations?

text_solutions: Ex situ conservation, such as captive breeding and botanical gardens, is used for critically endangered species with small populations.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about invasive species is incorrect?

options.text: Invasive species always have a positive effect on ecosystems.
Lantana camara is an example of an invasive species in India.

text_solutions: Invasive species often harm native biodiversity by competing for resources, altering habitats, and disrupting ecological interactions.

qns_content.text: Which scientist first isolated DNA and named it ‘Nuclein’?

text_solutions: Friedrich Miescher first isolated DNA in 1869 and named it ‘Nuclein’.

qns_content.text: Which characteristic is common to both liverworts and hornworts?

text_solutions: Both liverworts and hornworts have a thalloid body structure, but only liverworts have gemma cups.

qns_content.text: Which type of root modification is observed in plants like Asparagus for storage of food?

text_solutions: Fasciculated roots, as seen in Asparagus, are swollen roots occurring in clusters and function in food storage.

qns_content.text: Which genetic principle is demonstrated when heterozygous individuals express a phenotype intermediate between the two homozygous parents?

text_solutions: Incomplete dominance occurs when heterozygous individuals show a phenotype that is intermediate between two homozygous parents, as seen in snapdragon flower color.

qns_content.text: Which of the following components is NOT directly involved in the process of translation?

text_solutions: DNA is not directly involved in translation; mRNA, tRNA, and ribosomes carry out protein synthesis.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about biodiversity conservation is correct?

options.text: In situ conservation protects species in their natural habitat
Ex situ conservation is always more effective than in situ conservation
Biodiversity hotspots are areas with low species richness
Sacred groves have no role in biodiversity conservation

text_solutions: In situ conservation involves protecting species in their natural habitats, such as in national parks and sanctuaries.

qns_content.text: What happens to energy as it moves up the trophic levels?

text_solutions: Energy decreases as it moves up the trophic levels due to energy loss as heat and metabolic activities, following the 10% law.

qns_content.text: Which type of blood cells in frogs are nucleated?

text_solutions: Unlike mammals, frog erythrocytes (RBCs) are nucleated and contain hemoglobin.

qns_content.text: Which condition is characterized by the destruction of alveolar walls, reducing the respiratory surface area?

text_solutions: Emphysema is a chronic disorder that damages the alveolar walls, reducing the surface area for gas exchange.

qns_content.text: What is the purpose of the antibiotic resistance gene in a plasmid vector?

text_solutions: Antibiotic resistance genes act as selectable markers, helping identify bacterial cells that have taken up the recombinant plasmid.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is correct about RNA interference (RNAi)?

options.text: RNAi silences gene expression using double-stranded RNA.
RNAi is used to amplify DNA sequences.

text_solutions: RNA interference (RNAi) silences specific gene expression by using double-stranded RNA molecules.

qns_content.text: Which organ is affected by elephantiasis?

text_solutions: Elephantiasis is caused by filarial worms and affects the lymphatic system, leading to severe swelling.

qns_content.text: Which organism is considered a living fossil, representing an ancient evolutionary lineage?

text_solutions: Coelacanth is considered a living fossil, representing an ancient group of lobe-finned fishes.

qns_content.text: Which hormone is secreted by the hypothalamus and inhibits the release of growth hormone?

text_solutions: Somatostatin, secreted by the hypothalamus, inhibits the release of growth hormone from the pituitary gland.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is incorrect about blood circulation?

options.text: Pulmonary circulation carries blood between the heart and lungs.
Systemic circulation delivers oxygenated blood to body tissues.
The right ventricle pumps oxygenated blood into the aorta.
The left atrium receives oxygenated blood from pulmonary veins.

text_solutions: The right ventricle pumps deoxygenated blood into the pulmonary artery, not the aorta.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is an example of a high-energy molecule used in cellular activities?

text_solutions: ATP and NADPH are high-energy molecules that provide energy for cellular activities.

qns_content.text: Which excretory organ is present in Annelida?

text_solutions: Nephridia are the excretory organs in annelids, helping in osmoregulation and waste removal.

qns_content.text: Which of the following conditions is caused by high levels of urea in the blood due to kidney failure?

text_solutions: Uremia is caused by kidney failure, leading to the accumulation of urea in the blood.

qns_content.text: What is the name of the first cervical vertebra?

text_solutions: The atlas is the first cervical vertebra, supporting the skull.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a correct statement about amniocentesis?

options.text: Amniocentesis is used to determine fetal genetic disorders.

text_solutions: Amniocentesis is a diagnostic technique used to detect genetic disorders in a developing fetus.

qns_content.text: Which mechanism of evolution involves the recombination of genes during gametogenesis?

text_solutions: Genetic recombination during gametogenesis increases genetic variability, contributing to evolution.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is correct about micropropagation?

options.text: Micropropagation produces genetically identical plants through tissue culture.
Micropropagation involves crossing two different plant species.
Micropropagation is used only in animal cell culture.

text_solutions: Micropropagation is a tissue culture technique used to produce large numbers of genetically identical plants from a single tissue or cell.

qns_content.text: Which among the following is NOT a mode of HIV transmission?

text_solutions: HIV is not transmitted through casual contact like shaking hands; it spreads through blood, sexual fluids, and contaminated needles.

qns_content.text: Which receptor mediates the classical genomic actions of estrogen in target tissues?

text_solutions: Estrogen receptor alpha (ERα) is a key mediator of estrogen’s genomic actions in target tissues, influencing gene expression and cell function.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is an example of a fibrous protein?

text_solutions: Collagen is a fibrous protein that provides structural support in connective tissues.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about the frog’s circulatory system is incorrect?

options.text: The ventricle receives both oxygenated and deoxygenated blood.

text_solutions: Frogs exhibit double circulation, meaning blood passes through the heart twice in one complete cycle.

qns_content.text: Which feature is shared by both annelids and arthropods?

text_solutions: Both annelids and arthropods exhibit metameric segmentation, where the body is divided into repetitive segments.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about pulmonary ventilation is incorrect?

options.text: Inspiration occurs when the diaphragm contracts and moves downward.
Intercostal muscles help in expanding the thoracic cavity during inhalation.

text_solutions: Normal expiration is a passive process that occurs due to the relaxation of respiratory muscles, not an active one.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about neurons is incorrect?

options.text: Neurons consist of a cell body, axon, and dendrites.

text_solutions: Neurons have limited regenerative ability and typically do not divide once they are mature.

qns_content.text: Which phase of the menstrual cycle is characterized by high progesterone levels and prepares the endometrium for potential implantation?

text_solutions: During the luteal phase, the corpus luteum secretes high levels of progesterone to thicken the endometrium for implantation.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is an essential feature of a cloning vector?

text_solutions: Antibiotic resistance genes in cloning vectors help in the selection of recombinant bacteria by allowing only transformed cells to survive.

qns_content.text: Which crop is genetically modified for improved vitamin A content?

text_solutions: Golden rice is genetically modified to produce beta-carotene, a precursor of vitamin A, to combat vitamin A deficiency.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is NOT a step in recombinant DNA technology?

text_solutions: SDS-PAGE is used for protein separation, whereas recombinant DNA technology involves DNA isolation, ligation, and transformation.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about histamine is correct?

options.text: Histamine is released by mast cells during an allergic reaction.
Histamine is not involved in immune responses.

text_solutions: Histamine is released by mast cells during allergic reactions and causes inflammation.

qns_content.text: Which hormone is responsible for increasing hunger?

text_solutions: Ghrelin, secreted by the stomach, stimulates hunger and increases food intake.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about polysaccharides is incorrect?

options.text: Starch is a storage polysaccharide in plants.
Glycogen is a structural polysaccharide in animals.
Chitin is a structural polysaccharide in arthropods.

text_solutions: Glycogen is a storage polysaccharide in animals, not a structural one.

qns_content.text: What type of circulatory system is found in arthropods?

text_solutions: Arthropods have an open circulatory system, where blood directly bathes tissues and organs.

qns_content.text: Which condition in females is associated with an absence of menstrual cycles due to lack of ovarian function?

text_solutions: Amenorrhea refers to the absence of menstruation, which can result from ovarian failure or dysfunction.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Hugo de Vries proposed the theory of natural selection.
Ozone layer formation allowed the survival of aquatic life only.
The formation of organic molecules in Miller’s experiment supported chemical evolution.
Homologous organs arise due to convergent evolution.

text_solutions: Miller’s experiment provided experimental support for the formation of organic molecules, supporting the theory of chemical evolution.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about Southern blotting is correct?

options.text: Southern blotting is used to detect specific DNA sequences.
Southern blotting does not require gel electrophoresis.
Southern blotting is used to study protein expression.
Southern blotting is not useful in genetic fingerprinting.

text_solutions: Southern blotting is a molecular biology technique used to detect specific DNA sequences in a sample.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is an essential step to prevent sexually transmitted infections (STIs)?

text_solutions: Avoiding multiple sexual partners and practicing safe sex (e.g., using condoms) are important preventive measures against STIs.

qns_content.text: Which protein prevents myosin from binding to actin in a relaxed muscle?

text_solutions: Tropomyosin covers myosin-binding sites on actin filaments in relaxed muscles, preventing contraction.

qns_content.text: Which condition results from the accumulation of uric acid crystals in joints?

text_solutions: Gout is caused by the accumulation of uric acid crystals in joints, leading to inflammation and pain.

qns_content.text: Which component of blood is mainly involved in blood clotting?

text_solutions: Platelets (thrombocytes) play a crucial role in blood clotting by forming a platelet plug at the site of injury.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements is correct about carbohydrates?

options.text: Monosaccharides are the simplest form of carbohydrates.

text_solutions: Monosaccharides are the simplest carbohydrates. Polysaccharides are made of sugar units, not nucleotides. Cellulose is structural, and sucrose is a disaccharide.

qns_content.text: Which part of the frog's reproductive system produces sperm?

text_solutions: The testes in male frogs produce sperm, which are released through the urinogenital duct.

qns_content.text: Which of the following animals is viviparous?

text_solutions: Macaca (monkey) is a mammal and is viviparous, meaning it gives birth to live young.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a characteristic of red muscle fibers?

text_solutions: Red muscle fibers are fatigue-resistant due to high myoglobin and abundant mitochondria, allowing sustained aerobic activity​.

qns_content.text: Which part of the brain is the largest and is involved in higher-order functions such as thinking and memory?

text_solutions: The cerebrum is the largest part of the brain and is responsible for higher cognitive functions like reasoning and memory.

qns_content.text: Which immune cells are responsible for antigen presentation to T-lymphocytes?

text_solutions: Macrophages act as antigen-presenting cells (APCs) by processing and displaying antigens to T-lymphocytes for immune response activation.

qns_content.text: What is the main advantage of using Bt toxin in genetically modified crops?

text_solutions: Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) toxin provides resistance to insect pests, reducing the need for chemical pesticides.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about Southern blotting is correct?

options.text: Southern blotting is used to detect specific DNA sequences.
Southern blotting is used to detect proteins.
Southern blotting does not require gel electrophoresis.
Southern blotting is not useful in genetic analysis.

text_solutions: Southern blotting is a molecular biology technique used to detect specific DNA sequences in a sample.
